question.prompt: When the natural numbers \(P\) and \(P',\) with \(P\gt P',\) are divided by the natural number \(D,\) the remainders are \(R\) and \(R',\) respectively. When \(PP'\) and \(RR'\) are divided by \(D,\) the remainders are \(r\) and \(r',\) respectively. Then:

solutions.explanation:
Since division by \(D\) is given, \(D>0\). Write the two divisions as
\[
P=qD+R,\qquad P'=q'D+R',
\]
where \(q,q'\) are nonnegative integers and \(0\le R,R'<D\). These expressions separate the multiples of \(D\), which contribute no remainder, from the remaining parts.

Also write
\[
RR'=tD+r',\qquad 0\le r'<D,
\]
where \(t\) is a nonnegative integer. Expanding the product gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
PP'&=(qD+R)(q'D+R')\\
&=D(qq'D+qR'+q'R)+RR'\\
&=D(qq'D+qR'+q'R+t)+r'.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last expression is a quotient-remainder representation of \(PP'\), because its quotient is a nonnegative integer and \(0\le r'<D\). Hence the remainder \(r\) must equal \(r'\). This also covers \(D=1\), when both remainders are zero. Therefore \(\boxed{r=r'\text{ always}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Write each number using its remainder
